transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... I keep hearing voices at work. I'm a nursing assistant, and lately, I've been hearing these voices coming from the call-light speaker, and sometimes the hallway vents. They tell me exactly which patient records have been changed. 

It sounds as clear as somebody standing right next to me talking, but... well, even when the unit is completely quiet, nobody else seems to hear it. Just me. So, that's why I came in.
When did you first start hearing these voices? Was it sudden, like it happened over a few days, or did it develop more gradually over weeks or months?

It has been going on for about two months now. It started right around the time I was asked to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout at work. I guess it was pretty sudden, because I just started noticing them right when all that new paperwork began.

Over the past two months, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling unusually happy, energetic, or irritable? And have you needed less sleep than usual, or felt like you could go on less sleep without feeling tired?

Well, yeah, actually. My mood has been... different. Some days I wake up and I just feel like I'm finally awake, you know? Like I have all this energy and I'm meant to fix everything at work with this new rollout. I feel really good, really driven. 

But then... if my husband tells me I need to rest, or if one of the nurses at work tells me to slow down, I just snap at them. I get really irritable, like they're trying to block something important that I'm supposed to be doing. It's like they just don't get it. As for sleep, I haven't been sleeping much at all, maybe a few hours a night, but I don't really feel tired. I just feel ready to keep going.

Over these past two months, has this feeling of being energized and driven been pretty much constant, or does it come and go—like some days you feel great and other days your mood drops back to normal or lower?

Well, it hasn't been completely constant the whole two months. I'd say... it comes and goes. Some days I wake up and I have all that energy and drive I was talking about, and I feel like I can just take on the world. But then there are other days where... I guess I just feel more like my regular self. The energy kind of drops back down to normal. I haven't really felt low or depressed or anything like that, just... back to baseline, I suppose.
When you're having those days with high energy and feeling driven, is that when you hear the voices most? Or do you hear them even on the days when your mood feels more normal?

Well, they definitely go together. I never heard those call-light voices, or... or saw the hidden messages in the patient charts before this whole period when I got so driven and wound up about the rollout. They really only started after I was sleeping less and working nonstop. You know, when I started feeling certain that I had to fix everything at the facility. So, yeah, I really only notice them when I'm having those high-energy days.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F20.1 (Paranoid schizophrenia) and F23 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder) because hallucinations are episodic and mood-congruent with elevated mood episodes, not independent psychotic symptoms. The clear temporal relationship between mood elevation, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and hallucinations that occur only during high-energy days is most consistent with Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic with psychotic features (F30.2).
